text:
The picture points to roughly mid-2015. Unemployment is 5.4%, headline CPI is slightly negative at -0.11% YoY, and fed funds is about 0.12%. The broad dollar is up about 12.9% YoY, which fits the 2015 dollar surge.

To narrow the month: 2-year yield at 0.62% and 10-year at 2.13% look like May or June 2015. Unemployment was 5.5% in May 2015 and 5.3% in June, and 5.4% was the value later reported for April and revised for other months. Headline CPI YoY was about -0.2% in April 2015, 0.0% in May and 0.1% in June, so -0.11 is close to a March–April reading, but data vintage could shift this.

The 10-year yield rose 0.13 over 3 months. It was about 1.9% in Feb 2015 and 2.2% in May and June. The 20y+ Treasury return of -2.2% for the month fits May or June 2015, as the bond selloff came in May and June. Emerging-market equity fell 5.6% in the month, which fits June–August 2015, but August would show a much higher VIX. Gold down 1.2% fits June. Payrolls averaged about 191k, consistent with a May–June reading. Industrial production YoY of +1.93% fits mid-2015, as does a core CPI of 1.81%. Overall I pick June 2015, though May is possible.
